clip_script:
Let us spend a Saturday with decimals. You have five hundred rand. On the list: three school shirts at forty-five rand fifty each and a pair of shoes at one hundred and twenty-three rand eighty. Before you shop, estimate. Three shirts at about forty-five is about one hundred and thirty-five. Shoes about one hundred and twenty-five. Together about two hundred and sixty. From five hundred, about two hundred and forty left. Now you know roughly what to expect at the till, and nobody can overcharge you by much without you noticing.

At the till, exact. Three times forty-five comma five zero: three times forty-five is one hundred and thirty-five, three times fifty cents is one rand fifty, so one hundred and thirty-six comma five zero. Add the shoes, commas lined up: one hundred and thirty-six comma five zero plus one hundred and twenty-three comma eight zero.
